absent: Scan engine internals: how references are discovered, what paint colors mean beyond grey, how unreferenced status is decided, and scan area handling.
Tracking record full layouts and allocation and free interception points, including object identity and lifetime rules.
Scan thread lifecycle details: creation, wakeup timing, stop semantics, and interaction of timing values with scheduling delays.
Sequential file traversal callbacks for start, advance and stop, and concurrency behavior for multiple readers.
List LRU internal helpers for shard resolution, insertion, deletion, walking, per node initialization, index management and shrinker signaling.
Memory cgroup accounting details: identifier allocation, private table management, root definition, folio charge flags and object extension lifetime.
Memblock range and flag helper semantics: merging, splitting, overlap handling, node assignment, flag encodings, resizing, allocation search and free paths.
Boot memory limits and direction: meaning of unrestricted upper bound, bottom up mode, mirror and hotplug effects, and architecture retention of reservation data.
Debugfs registration context, permission enforcement, cleanup workqueue context, module lifetime and error origin details.
Numeric encodings for poison patterns, page frame bound initialization timing, contiguous node setup and scratch only usage.

findings.text: Leak report iteration exposes one tracked allocation per record. Display is limited to entries already marked reported that remain without references at show time, evaluated while holding the entry private lock with interrupts preserved. All other entries produce no output but still succeed.

Sequential report facility ties four traversal callbacks to a single table and attaches that table to each opened control file, so every reader shares the same start, advance, stop and display behavior.

Address triggered diagnostic accepts a numeric string and probes normal, physical and per cpu accounting domains for the same value, emitting detailed information for each match found while holding the relevant entry lock. Absence in all domains yields an informational message and an invalid argument result; malformed numbers also fail as invalid argument.

Clear operation transitions every reported yet unreferenced entry back to grey and resets the global leak found indicator to false. Traversal occurs under read side protection with per entry interrupt disabling exclusion for the flag evaluation and recoloring.

Control channel accepts at most one textual directive per write, using only a bounded prefix of user input with guaranteed termination. Access is serialized by an interruptible scan mutex. Successful handling consumes the full offered length for file position purposes; failures propagate without position change. Clear is honored even when the detector is disabled by invoking the disabled state reclamation path.

Supported directives cover clearing, permanent disabling, toggling of stack scanning, enabling or disabling periodic scanning, configuring the scan period in seconds, triggering an immediate scan, and dumping a single address. All except clear require the detector to be enabled, otherwise permission is denied, and unrecognized input is rejected as invalid argument.

Interval configuration converts seconds to the internal tick unit with saturation at the maximum unsigned value, halts periodic activity before applying the new period, and restarts it only when the resulting wait is nonzero. Parse failures leave prior timing untouched.

Disabled state reclamation assumes exclusive access and therefore walks the global object registry without read side or global locking, removing and deleting every entry. It yields the processor periodically to avoid prolonged nonpreemptible execution.
Detector control file offers open, sequential read, write, reposition and release operations under module ownership, with reads and positioning delegated to generic sequential file helpers.

Asynchronous disable halts periodic scanning, then clears the free tracking enable under mutex protection with ordering ensured by thread stop. When no leaks were recorded it reclaims all internal tracking state; otherwise it retains that state and directs the operator to use the clear directive for reclamation.

Early boot option recognizes only on and off. Off disables the detector immediately; on suppresses automatic disable under default off builds and requests early initialization of the stack depot. Missing or other values fail as invalid argument.

Early initialization is skipped when default off applies without override or when a prior error was recorded. Otherwise it establishes minimum age and scan wait timing, creates untraced caches for tracking records and scan areas, and registers static data, zero initialized data and possibly read only after init regions as grey atomic allocations.

Late initialization marks the subsystem ready, publishes the control file in debugfs, and on prior error schedules asynchronous cleanup while reporting out of memory. When automatic scanning is configured it starts the periodic thread under mutex protection and unconditionally logs pool availability.

A dedicated mutex guards the registry of memory cgroup aware LRU instances and any walk over that registry for teardown or reparenting. Registration and unregistration acquire it only for aware instances.

Registry maintenance is conditional: aware instances are linked or unlinked under lock, unaware instances bypass the global list entirely, and builds without cgroup support provide empty operations with identical signatures.

Per shard access offers interrupt disabling and interrupt state preserving variants that resolve the shard for a node and cgroup context through a shared helper, with matching unlock operations restoring the prior interrupt state.

Insertion service locks the target shard, attempts to add the supplied queue element, unlocks and reports whether the element was newly added. The address derived variant infers the node from the containing page and, for aware instances only, infers the cgroup from the address under read side protection.

Cgroup ownership of an arbitrary address is null when accounting is disabled. Slab addresses consult per object extension data; all other addresses consult the folio association with null tolerance for uncharged pages.

Per object slab ownership requires both extension storage and an accounting needy cache. Lookup holds a temporary reference on the extension block across object and cgroup resolution and releases it on all paths, returning null when either storage or association is absent.
Removal service mirrors insertion for node and cgroup inference, including read side protection for aware instances, and reports whether the element was present.

Detachment primitives both decrement the source shard occupancy. One leaves the element isolated; the other requeues it onto a caller supplied head while still accounting it as removed from the shard.

Occupancy queries tolerate missing shards and transient negative observations by reporting zero in those cases. Single shard reads occur under read side protection; whole node aggregates use an atomic read of the node counter.

Reclamation walk covers one shard with interrupt protection or a whole node without it. Node scope always visits the root shard first and then, while budget remains and awareness applies, iterates the cgroup index acquiring a reference on each cgroup for the duration of its shard visit.
Translation from cgroup private identifier to cgroup reference performs an indexed lookup and requires the caller to already hold read side protection, enforced by a one time warning.

Cgroup awareness lifecycle: initialization enables an interrupt safe index and records the awareness flag, teardown frees all indexed per cgroup structures, and offline reparenting migrates each per node queue to the parent, transfers occupancy, flags the destination shrinker, marks the source dead with a sentinel, erases the index and defers final release until read side grace. Builds without cgroup support leave both operations empty.

Reparenting serializes instances with the global registry mutex and orders shard spinlocks source before destination with nesting annotation, using interrupt disabling acquisition on the source. Marking the source dead precedes index erasure to prevent concurrent deletion from corrupting either queue.

Folio driven shard provisioning is a no operation for unaware instances, succeeds immediately when the shard already exists as observed under read side protection, and otherwise pins the folio cgroup across a potentially blocking allocation before releasing the pin.

Pinned folio ownership yields null when accounting is disabled and the root cgroup when the folio carries no charge. Charged folios are resolved under read side protection with a retry loop until a stable reference is obtained.

Instance lifecycle records shrinker identity or a negative sentinel when no shrinker applies, forces unawareness when kernel memory accounting is disabled, allocates and initializes per node shards, enables the cgroup index and registers the instance. Teardown reverses registration and frees cgroup and node state while resetting identity; allocation failure during setup reports out of memory.
Teardown is idempotent with respect to absent initialization: a null node pointer causes immediate return without further action.
Static capacity facts: memory table 128 entries, reserved table 128 entries, physical memory table 4 entries.

Early memory descriptor aggregates a memory region set and a reserved region set, each with a static array, capacity and human readable name, plus allocation direction and an unrestricted upper bound. A distinct physical memory descriptor carries its own small static array, capacity and name.

Boot time globals provide a contiguous node descriptor, low and high page frame bounds including a 64 bit possible maximum, and a scratch only indicator that is a mutable flag in one configuration and a constant false in the other.

Auxiliary boot state holds debug enablement, a mirror presence flag, growth permission, and slab placement markers for the two main region tables, with a query operation exposing only whether any mirrored range exists.

Discard phase releases only grown region tables, distinguishing slab allocated from early allocated storage for the appropriate free path with page aligned sizing, and clears the indirection to the memory set to prevent further use.

Range management entry points add with explicit node and flags, add with default placement, remove from the memory set, add to the physical set, and mark hotplug or mirror attributes. All forward to shared range or flag helpers and emit tracing diagnostics including caller identity.
Mirror marking has no effect unless mirrored kernel core support is enabled. When enabled it records system wide mirror presence before delegating to the flag helper.

Reserved area release converts virtual bounds to physical form with kernel symbol awareness and end inclusive handling, optionally unreserves the interval when the architecture retains memblock data, frees the underlying pages with caller chosen poisoning, and logs the reclaimed size when a label is supplied.

Leak detector exclusion combines per entry interrupt preserving spin protection for flag checks and reporting, a global scan mutex for control directives and thread lifecycle, and read side critical sections for registry traversal.

Shard organization pairs per node aggregates holding an atomic total with per shard queues each holding a list, a spinlock and a signed occupancy count, indexed by node and by cgroup with an associated shrinker identity.

Control vocabulary facts: clear, off, stack equals on, stack equals off, scan equals on, scan equals off, scan equals value, bare scan, dump equals value. Matching is by prefix on the bounded input and only the first directive per write is honored.

Control input facts: staging holds 64 bytes with 63 usable for directive selection and guaranteed termination; the remainder of the offered length is ignored for selection but counted as consumed on success.
Published control file facts: debugfs name kmemleak with mode 0644.
Concurrent disable paths may schedule duplicate cleanup work; serialization relies on the shared scan mutex rather than exclusion of scheduling itself.

Dead shard sentinel uses the most negative long value; occupancy transfer warns on negative source counts before merging, and further allocations for dying cgroups are avoided via a dying state check.
